name: opkssh-7d4029f4-blind30-ots
instr:
# opkssh: thirty behavioural regressions to find without a test suite

This tool lets a person sign in with an identity issuer and use the signed credential that comes back to reach a secure-shell server, and it lets an operator record on disk who is allowed in. Several things went wrong at once after an unreviewed batch of changes landed, and the symptoms span almost everything a person does with it. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.

Signing in is where it starts. When the sign-in is asked to carry the issuer's access credential inside the signed material it produces, the finished credential holds none of it and reading it back yields empty text; when the sign-in is not asked for one, an empty access field is present that should not be there. Printing that signed material for a human to read is broken twice over: the section that walks the embedded signed proof — its body, the issuer's signature and the client's signature — either never appears or makes the whole printout come back as a failure, and the closing summary of issuer, intended recipient, subject, identity, hash and signing algorithm is likewise missing. In the same printout, a credential with no start date is shown as a 1970 date rather than the words meaning the field was never set, while the value meaning "never expires" still prints as forever.
